title: Customer IaC blueprints: variable mapping, module composition, and overlay patterns for Private VPC deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers run private VPC deployments with divergent terraform customizations (brand networking, custom DNS, bespoke IAM roles, external integrations). We need a minimal-but-extensible IaC blueprint approach so we can ship a managed Private product that is maintainable across upgrades and supports safe customer-specific overlays without forking our core modules.

Scope: produce a reference blueprint and composition guidelines documenting patterns for: 1) variable mapping and stability guarantees (public vs internal variables), 2) overlay mechanisms (patch files, tfvars layering, module wrappers), 3) composing our core modules with customer modules, 4) upgrade hooks and migration steps for customers, 5) automated health checks and drift detection hooks integrated into our deploy pipeline.

Goal: reduce initial integration time for new Private customers by 40% and eliminate >80% of ad-hoc one-off terraform forks by providing a recommended, audited composition pattern and tooling (scripts + CI checks).
acceptance_criteria: Reference blueprint repo with example compositions for 3 common customer patterns: minimal (shared VPC), proxied-egress (private subnet + NAT), and restricted services (custom IAM + endpoint policies)
Documentation describing variable categorization: stable_public, stable_internal, customer_override, and volatile/runtime; guidance for which variables can be safely overridden in overlays
A lightweight overlay tool (shell + small Go binary) that applies ordered tfvar layers and validates no disallowed state changes before plan/apply
Upgrade strategy doc describing preflight checks, state migration steps, and a canary flow for module version upgrades with rollback hooks
Two CI checks: (a) drift-detection terraform plan compare against golden baseline, (b) health-check smoke tests after apply that exercise control plane API and network paths
Internal RFC and sign-off from Security (SRO), Product, and Platform owners
comments: 2026-02-21 — Kickoff: scoped blueprint repo and listed 3 customer archetypes. Action: Rafael to draft example composition for shared VPC pattern.

2026-02-26 — Design review with PM (Aisha Patel): agreed to use layered tfvars + small wrapper to avoid forcing customers into special tooling. PM requested a minimal wrapper approach rather than a heavy templating engine.

2026-03-02 — Eng sync: decided variable categories and rules. Trade-off: allowing customer_override for networking fields increases upgrade complexity; mitigation is an automated preflight planner that detects disallowed drift on upgrade.

2026-03-05 — Security review: initial concerns about customer-supplied IAM module composition. Security requested explicit safelists and a tightened audit step; Rafael to add policy validation with tfsec + custom checks.
2026-03-10 — Prototype: initial overlay tool (apply-tfvars) implemented; example composition for proxied-egress pattern added to repo. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-iac/pull/17
2026-03-12 — Blocker noted: Terraform state import/migration story for customers that already forked modules. Adding migration playbook and support task to onboarding checklist.
decision_log: Prefer layering tfvars and small wrapper over generating full terraform via templating (reduced cognitive and operational cost for customers)
Categorize variables into 4 buckets to constrain what customers can override and to simplify upgrade compatibility checks
Implement preflight plan validation as a gating step on module upgrades to prevent inadvertent resource replacements in customer accounts
implementation_notes: Core modules must declare a stable_inputs metadata block (docstring + tags) for variables intended as stable_public. We'll add a module linter that fails CI if stability annotations are missing.

Overlay tool will apply layers in this order: base_terraform -> redwood_overrides -> customer_tfvars -> secretized_vars. Each layer validated with terraform plan -out and scanned by custom policy checks.

For upgrades, publish a migration module that can be applied in a read-only 'preview' mode to detect any resource address changes. If preview shows replacements, notify customer and provide step-by-step migration commands.

Health checks implemented as a Post-Apply job in CI that runs: (1) control-plane API key auth, (2) sample generate call against local endpoint, (3) VPC egress test to configured external endpoint. Failures create a release-blocking incident ticket.
Add a small 'compose' example in repo showing how to wrap core module 'redwood_vpc' with customer 'corp_network' module without duplicating provider or backend blocks.
next_steps: Finish example composition for restricted-services archetype (due 2026-03-18)
Add tfsec and custom IAM safelist checks into CI pipeline (owner: Security Eng)
Publish RFC and run stakeholder sign-off (SRE, Security, PM) by 2026-03-20
Create onboarding checklist entry and migration playbook for customers with existing forks
